age-group-record.short: The best result ever recorded in an age class of masters sport, such as men aged 70–74. Records show what the best can do at each age, not what a typical athlete does.

lifelong-exerciser.short: A person who has trained regularly for most of adult life. In the study here they had exercised about 5 days a week for 52 years.

sarcopenia.short: The age-related loss of muscle mass. Strength usually falls faster than mass, so size alone understates the loss.

dynapenia.short: The loss of muscle strength with age. It is a more consistent risk for disability and death than the loss of muscle mass.

anabolic-resistance.short: A weaker build-up of muscle protein in older muscle after protein or resistance exercise, though resting turnover is about the same.
